title: X.509 certificate (DER) structure
summary: An X.509 v3 certificate is a DER-encoded (ASN.1) structure: TBSCertificate (to-be-signed: version, serial number, signature algorithm, issuer, validity, subject, subject public key info, extensions), signature algorithm identifier, and the signature value. The whole is wrapped in a SEQUENCE.

ext.summary: An X.509 v3 certificate is a DER-encoded (ASN.1) structure: TBSCertificate (to-be-signed: version, serial number, signature algorithm, issuer, validity, subject, subject public key info, extensions), signature algorithm identifier, and the signature value. The whole is wrapped in a SEQUENCE.

structure.meaning: Outer SEQUENCE wrapping tbsCertificate, signatureAlgorithm, signatureValue.

SEQUENCE: version [0] (v3), serialNumber INTEGER, signature AlgorithmIdentifier, issuer Name, validity (notBefore, notAfter), subject Name, subjectPublicKeyInfo, issuerUniqueID [1], subjectUniqueID [2], extensions [3].
AlgorithmIdentifier (OID + parameters) for the signature (e.g. sha256WithRSAEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11).
BIT STRING containing the signature bytes.

ext.example_decoded: DER prefix: SEQUENCE { SEQUENCE { [0] version v3, serial 1, sig alg sha256WithRSAEncryption ... } }
notes: DER is the canonical subset of BER (X.690) used for certificates and signatures.
Serial number must be positive (high bit cleared) and unique per issuer.
Subject/issuer are Distinguished Names (DN) as RDNSequence (C, O, OU, CN, ...).
Extensions: subjectAltName (SAN), keyUsage, extendedKeyUsage, basicConstraints (CA:TRUE/FALSE), authorityKeyIdentifier, subjectKeyIdentifier.
Signature covers the DER encoding of tbsCertificate.
